Someone wanted a line to him that I'd never see.
He gets twenty bucks a week from me and it all goes on skate wax and game stuff.

I keep picturing him on the road with his hood up, no idea where he'll sleep.

Theo has never even asked to go to camp without me. He wouldn't just go for nothing.
What did she promise him if he came?

onboarding.text: I came off a twelve-hour night shift to find Marcus at my door holding Theo's backpack. He'd found it at the Northgate skate park with Theo's phone still inside. Theo was supposed to be at Marcus's. He never showed.
onboarding.label: Dana

onboarding.text: It's been just the two of us for two years. Drive-thru breakfast after my shifts, him narrating every trick he landed while I tried to stay awake. He used to tell me everything.
onboarding.label: Dana & Theo

onboarding.text: Theo is fifteen. Skater, gamer, all elbows and headphones. Quiet with adults, fiercely loyal to his friends. All summer he's been glued to that phone, grinning at something he wouldn't show me.
onboarding.label: Theo

onboarding.text: The police took a report and told me teenagers usually turn up. Usually. I'm not waiting on usually. I can't make sense of his phone, but you can. Help me find my son.
onboarding.label: Dana
